roles.definition: Defines or analyzes concepts, formal properties or explanatory theory.
sufficient_for: research proposal when bound to the exact theoretical claim

roles.definition: Defines a computational or analytical method, its assumptions, operations or complexity.
sufficient_for: candidate method contract when the exact algorithmic claim is located

roles.definition: Provides component, boundary, interface, lifecycle or deployment structure evidence.
Provides normative requirements or controlled vocabulary from an identified standards authority.
sufficient_for: candidate conformance obligations within the standard's exact scope

roles.definition: Reports observations, experiments, benchmarks or measured outcomes relevant to a bounded claim.
sufficient_for: empirical support within the studied population and method

roles.definition: Provides evidence about human work, cognition, accessibility, interaction, safety or organizational behavior.
Defines authority, accountability, assurance, policy, risk, privacy, security or audit obligations.
sufficient_for: candidate governance constraints within its issuing scope

roles.definition: Helps falsify merge, split, demotion, externalization or ownership decisions for a product boundary.
sufficient_for: candidate boundary adjudication when independent lifecycle and negative evidence are present

roles.definition: Shows that an independently operated product, project or organization addresses some related job or capability.
sufficient_for: discovering candidate needs, seams or provider patterns

roles.definition: Describes a concrete provider, project, API, runtime or technical implementation.
sufficient_for: candidate provider contract and implementation pattern research

roles.definition: Explicit debt used when committed metadata cannot defensibly assign a narrower controlled role.
sufficient_for: preserving the source for later review
not_sufficient_for: any semantic, implementation, qualification or acceptance gate

assignment_laws: A source may serve multiple roles for different bounded claims.
A role applies to a source-claim binding, not permanently to the source.
Independent products are adoption evidence, never default semantic authority.
